sense: the righteous is generous and gives
operation: the wicked borrows and does not repay, but the righteous is generous and gives - open-handedness as a mark of the righteous interior
discovery: v21: 'the RIGHTEOUS is GENEROUS and gives' - the operation is open-handed giving; the righteous interior is marked by a freedom to give that the grasping wicked lacks.

coupling: the graciousness for which God blessed him
discovery: 'GRACE (chen) is poured upon your lips' — the king's gracious, winsome speech; chen = favour/charm, the gracious character expressed in his words, for which God has blessed him forever (the blessing = qualifier)

'hide not yourself from my SUPPLICATION (techinnah)' — the plea for grace the psalmist casts on God; techinnah (appeal for favour) the humbled cry that expects nothing by right, only mercy — the posture beneath the prayer

sense: pity / have compassion (chus - he has pity on the weak)
discovery: 'He has PITY (chus) on the weak and the needy' — the tenderness of the just king; chus here the compassion that spares and cares for the weak - the inward mercy behind the king's saving acts, kingship marked by pity, not merely power

locus: paired with holding her stones dear
discovery: v14: 'and have PITY (chanan) on her dust' - the tender regard of the servants for ruined Zion, love for her very dust.

locus: paired with God's compassion on those who fear him
discovery: v13: 'As a father SHOWS COMPASSION (racham) to his children' - the tender pity of a human father, the analogy for God's mercy.
v12: 'nor any to PITY (chanan) his fatherless children' - the wish that the pitiless find no pity for his own.

locus: paired with none to pity his children
discovery: v12: 'Let there be none to extend KINDNESS (chesed) to him' - the wish that the merciless man find no mercy.

locus: paired with the failure to remember
discovery: v16: 'did not remember to show KINDNESS (chesed)' - the mercy the enemy withheld, the root of his condemnation.

locus: paired with being merciful and righteous
discovery: v4: 'he is GRACIOUS (chanun), merciful, and righteous' - the God-fearer mirrors God's own grace toward others.
v4: 'gracious, MERCIFUL (rachum), and righteous' - the compassion of the God-fearer, God's mercy reflected in the man.

locus: paired with conducting affairs with justice
discovery: v5: 'It is well with the man who DEALS GENEROUSLY (chanan) and lends' - the open-handed generosity of the God-fearer.

locus: paired with the love and calling
discovery: v1: 'he has heard my voice and my PLEAS FOR MERCY (tachanun)' - the supplications God heard, the cry that drew forth love.
v2: 'be attentive to the voice of my PLEAS FOR MERCY (tachanun)!' - the supplication, the cry sharpened into a plea for grace.

operation: the psalmist lifts a crying voice of supplication, the cry as the counter-move to the schemes
discovery: v6: 'give ear to the voice of my PLEAS for mercy' - against the silent scheming, the psalmist's interior goes vocal, appealing upward.

operation: a righteous man's blow/rebuke is welcomed as kindness, oil for the head - correction embraced
discovery: v5: 'Let a righteous man strike me - it is a KINDNESS; let him rebuke me - it is oil for my head' - the operation is rare: the interior wants to be corrected, receiving reproof as care.
